'''Robert Sacre''' ({{birth date|1989|6|6}}) is a Canadian [[college basketball]] player from [[North Vancouver, British Columbia]].   He is currently a Senior at [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga University]] and is also a member of the [[Canada national men's basketball team|Canadian national basketball team]].

==Junior career==
Sacre was one of the top junior players in Canada.  In his junior season, he led [[Handsworth Secondary School]] to the British Columbia Provincial Championship; he was named MVP of the title game after scoring 17 points, grabbing 12 rebounds, and blocking four shots.<ref>[http://www.gozags.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=627536&SPID=90846&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=26400&ATCLID=205173769&Q_SEASON=2011] at gozags.com</ref>  In his senior season, he averaged 25 points, 12 rebounds, and four blocks per game while committing to play [[NCAA]] basketball with [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga University]].

As a junior player, he participated with the Canadian Junior National team at the 2005 Global Games and 2006 World Championship qualifiers.

==College career==
Sacre committed to [[NCAA]] Division I squad [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga University]] prior to the 2007-08 season.<ref>[http://espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=36392 Robert Sacre] at ESPN.com</ref>  He came off the bench in his freshman season, averaging nine minutes of action per game in 2007-08.  In 2008-09, he broke his foot three games into the season and was later granted a medical redshirt.  

Sacre came back strong in the 2009-10 season,averaging 10.3 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 1.9 blocks per game as the Bulldogs' starting center.<ref>[http://espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=36392 Profile] at ESPN.com</ref>

==International career==
Sacre played several tournaments for the Canadian junior team.  He averaged 9 points, 8.2 rebounds, and 3 blocks per game at the 2006 [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]], helping the Canadians to a fourth place finish in the tournament.<ref>[http://turkey2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/56482/pid2//sid/3931/tid/257/tid2//_/2006_FIBA_Americas_U18_Championship_for_Men/index.html Robert Sacre] at archive.FIBA.com</ref>

Sacre was called to the senior national team for the first time to participate at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]] in [[Turkey]].<ref>[http://turkey2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/10/fwcm/player/p/eid/4728/pid/56482/rid//sid/4728/tid/257/profile.html Robert Sacre] at FIBA.com</ref>

==Personal==
Sacre's father is former NFL tight-end [[Greg LaFleur]].
